subject: chemistry_2
question_text: What happens when white phosphorus is heated with conc. NaOH solution in an inert atmosphere of CO₂?

verification.note: Unit 7 (VA Group Elements) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.83-84, from the shaded sub-box "VA GROUP ELEMENTS" of printed chapter 7 ("7. VA, VIA, VIIA GROUP ELEMENTS & NOBLE GASES"); the book prints this question and a model answer on book p.83 as VSAQ 12. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK CHECK (book p.83, VSAQ 12): the printed equation P₄ + 3NaOH + 3H₂O → 3NaH₂PO₂ + PH₃ was atom-counted and IS balanced (P 4, Na 3, O 6, H 9 on both sides) and matches NCERT. BOOK GAP: the printed answer repeats the question's own condition, "in inert atmosphere of CO₂", without saying why the CO₂ is needed — to keep air out, because the phosphine produced contains traces of P₂H₄ which ignites in air. It also never names the products in words, and never says that the reaction is a disproportionation. All three are added.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The balanced equation
lines: The reaction is carried out in an inert
steps.why: The equation is the answer to a "what happens" question, and it must balance: four phosphorus atoms on the left become three in the hypophosphite and one in the phosphine. The condition line matters too, because the same reagents in air would give a different result.
common_mistakes: Writing PH₃ as the only product. Sodium hypophosphite, NaH₂PO₂, is formed at the same time.
Leaving out the 3H₂O. Without the water the hydrogen atoms do not balance.
steps.memory_tip: One P₄ needs 3NaOH and 3H₂O, and gives 3 salt plus 1 gas.
steps.margin_note: One balanced equation earns this mark. Check the hydrogen count before moving on: 9 on each side.

steps.label: Products and the CO₂ atmosphere
lines: The products are phosphine gas, PH₃, and

lines.text: P goes from 0 to −3 and to +1 at once.

lines: So this is a disproportionation reaction.
The CO₂ keeps air out, because the PH₃
contains traces of P₂H₄ that ignite in air.
steps.why: Naming the two products in words and giving the two oxidation numbers shows what kind of reaction it is: the same element is both oxidised and reduced, which is disproportionation. The CO₂ is there only to keep oxygen away from a gas that would otherwise catch fire as it leaves the flask.
common_mistakes: Calling NaH₂PO₂ sodium phosphite. It is sodium hypophosphite; sodium phosphite would be Na₂HPO₃.
Saying the CO₂ takes part in the reaction. It appears in no equation; it only keeps air away.
steps.memory_tip: One element, two directions: down to −3 in PH₃ and up to +1 in NaH₂PO₂.
steps.margin_note: The word disproportionation is worth writing. It is the one term that shows the reaction was understood.

insider_note: The book copies the CO₂ condition from the question without explaining it. Write the reason — the phosphine contains P₂H₄, which ignites in air — because that is the line an examiner reads as understanding rather than copying.
